answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one pearl weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, an hostile operator who spins up 242 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 298 times the capital for one share. The glacier report makes public the merge explicitly at each bridge. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 37 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
